question: What is the function of the air compressor in a commercial vehicle's air brake system?
choice_a: It pumps air into the air storage tanks (reservoirs)
choice_b: It releases compressed air from the brake chambers
choice_c: It regulates the parking brake spring tension
choice_d: It measures the vehicle's stopping distance
explanation: The manual states the air compressor pumps air into the air storage tanks (reservoirs) and is connected to the engine through gears or a v-belt.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.1 — Air Compressor

question: According to the manual, at approximately what pressure does the air compressor governor "cut-out," stopping the compressor from pumping air?
choice_a: 60 psi
choice_b: 125 psi
choice_c: 100 psi
choice_d: 150 psi
explanation: The governor stops the compressor from pumping air when tank pressure rises to the cut-out level, around 125 psi.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.1 — Air Compressor Governor

question: What does the air compressor governor control?
choice_a: When the parking brake spring releases
choice_b: When the stop light switch engages
choice_c: When the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks
choice_d: When the alcohol evaporator activates
explanation: The governor controls when the air compressor will pump air into the air storage tanks.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.1 — Air Compressor Governor

question: What feature is available on automatic air tanks to help prevent freezing of the automatic drain in cold weather?
choice_a: A backup mechanical drain
choice_b: An insulated tank jacket
choice_c: A secondary alcohol tank
choice_d: Electric heating devices
explanation: Automatic air tanks are available with electric heating devices that help prevent freezing of the automatic drain in cold weather.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.1 — Air Tanks

question: What is the purpose of an alcohol evaporator in an air brake system?
choice_a: To put alcohol into the air system to reduce the risk of ice in valves and other parts during cold weather
choice_b: To lubricate the air compressor
choice_c: To cool the compressed air before it enters the tanks
choice_d: To increase the governor cut-out pressure
explanation: Some air brake systems have an alcohol evaporator to put alcohol into the air system, reducing the risk of ice in air brake valves during cold weather.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.1.5 — Alcohol Evaporator

question: During cold weather, how often should you check the alcohol container and fill it as necessary?
choice_a: Once a week
choice_b: Every day
choice_c: Once a month
choice_d: Only before the first freeze of the season
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to check the alcohol container and fill up as necessary every day during cold weather.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.1.5 — Alcohol Evaporator

question: Where is the safety relief valve installed in an air brake system?
choice_a: In the brake pedal (foot valve) assembly
choice_b: In the parking brake control lever
choice_c: In the first tank the air compressor pumps air to
choice_d: In the alcohol evaporator container
explanation: A safety relief valve is installed in the first tank the air compressor pumps air to, protecting the tank and system from too much pressure.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.1.6 — Safety Valve

question: The safety relief valve is usually set to open at what pressure?
choice_a: 100 psi
choice_b: 125 psi
choice_c: 60 psi
choice_d: 150 psi
explanation: The manual states the safety valve is usually set to open at 150 psi.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.1.6 — Safety Valve

question: If the safety valve releases air, what does the manual instruct you to do?
choice_a: Have the fault fixed by a mechanic
choice_b: Add more alcohol to the evaporator
choice_c: Manually reset the governor
choice_d: Ignore it unless it happens twice in a row
explanation: If the safety valve releases air, something is wrong, and the manual says to have the fault fixed by a mechanic.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.1.6 — Safety Valve

question: The brake pedal in an air brake system is also known by what other names?
choice_a: The wig wag and stab valve
choice_b: The foot valve or treadle valve
choice_c: The push-pull knob and modulating lever
choice_d: The slack adjuster and s-cam
explanation: The manual notes the brake pedal is also called the foot valve or treadle valve.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.1.7 — The Brake Pedal

question: Why does the manual caution against unnecessarily pressing and releasing the brake pedal?
choice_a: It can damage the stop light switch
choice_b: It can freeze the alcohol evaporator
choice_c: It can let air out of the system faster than the compressor can replace it
choice_d: It can trigger the ABS malfunction lamp
explanation: Pressing and releasing the pedal unnecessarily can let air out faster than the compressor can replace it, and if pressure gets too low, the brakes won't work.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.1.7 — The Brake Pedal

question: What is the most common type of foundation brake used at each wheel?
choice_a: The wedge brake
choice_b: The air-operated disc brake
choice_c: The power-screw brake
choice_d: The s-cam drum brake
explanation: Foundation brakes are used at each wheel, and the most common type is the s-cam drum brake.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.1.8 — Foundation Brakes

question: In an s-cam drum brake, what happens as air pressure moves the slack adjuster and twists the brake camshaft?
choice_a: The s-cam forces the brake shoes apart against the inside of the drum
choice_b: The safety valve opens to relieve pressure
choice_c: The alcohol evaporator activates
choice_d: The application pressure gauge resets to zero
explanation: Turning the s-cam forces the brake shoes away from one another and presses them against the inside of the brake drum.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.1.8 — Foundation Brakes

question: In a wedge brake, what does the brake chamber push rod do?
choice_a: Twists the brake camshaft
choice_b: Pushes a wedge directly between the ends of two brake shoes
choice_c: Turns a power screw
choice_d: Opens the safety relief valve
explanation: In wedge brakes, the brake chamber push rod pushes a wedge directly between the ends of two brake shoes, shoving them apart against the drum.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.1.8 — Foundation Brakes

question: What does the supply pressure gauge connected to the air tank tell you?
choice_a: How much air pressure you are applying to the brakes
choice_b: The rate of brake fade
choice_c: How much pressure is in the air tanks
choice_d: The governor's cut-in pressure setting
explanation: All vehicles with air brakes have a pressure gauge connected to the air tank that tells you how much pressure is in the air tanks.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.1.9 — Supply Pressure Gauges

question: What does the application pressure gauge (not found on all vehicles) show?
choice_a: How much pressure is stored in the tanks
choice_b: The alcohol evaporator fluid level
choice_c: The compressor's cut-out pressure
choice_d: How much air pressure you are applying to the brakes
explanation: The application pressure gauge shows how much air pressure you are applying to the brakes.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.1.10 — Application Pressure Gauge

question: A visible low air pressure warning signal must come on before the air pressure in the tanks falls below what level?
choice_a: 60 psi
choice_b: 45 psi
choice_c: 100 psi
choice_d: 125 psi
explanation: A warning signal you can see must come on before the air pressure in the tanks falls below 60 psi.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.1.11 — Low Air Pressure Warning

question: What is the "wig wag" warning device?
choice_a: A gauge needle that turns red
choice_b: A mechanical arm that drops into your view when system pressure drops below 60 psi
choice_c: A buzzer wired to the parking brake
choice_d: A dashboard light that only appears at startup
explanation: The wig wag is a device that drops a mechanical arm into your view when the pressure in the system drops below 60 psi.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.1.11 — Low Air Pressure Warning

question: On large buses, the low pressure warning devices commonly signal at what pressure range?
explanation: The manual notes that on large buses it is common for the low pressure warning devices to signal at 80-85 psi.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.1.11 — Low Air Pressure Warning

question: How does the air brake system turn on the brake lights when the driver applies the brakes?
choice_a: Through a cable linked to the parking brake
choice_b: Through the ABS control module
choice_c: Through the alcohol evaporator circuit
choice_d: Through an electric switch that works by air pressure
explanation: The stop light switch is an electric switch that works by air pressure and turns on the brake lights when you apply the air brakes.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.1.12 — Stop Light Switch

question: Front brake limiting valves are found on vehicles made before what year, per the manual?
explanation: Some older vehicles made before 1975 have a front brake limiting valve and a control in the cab.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.1.13 — Front Brake Limiting Valve

question: Putting the front brake limiting valve control in the "slippery" position does what?
choice_a: Increases front brake pressure to maximum
choice_b: Cuts the normal air pressure to the front brakes by half
choice_c: Disables the rear brakes entirely
choice_d: Activates the alcohol evaporator
explanation: In the "slippery" position, the limiting valve cuts the normal air pressure to the front brakes by half.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.1.13 — Front Brake Limiting Valve

question: Automatic front wheel limiting valves reduce air to the front brakes except when the brakes are applied with how much pressure or more?
choice_a: 20 psi
choice_b: 45 psi
choice_c: 60 psi
choice_d: 100 psi
explanation: Automatic front wheel limiting valves reduce air to the front brakes except when the brakes are applied very hard, at 60 psi or more application pressure.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.1.13 — Front Brake Limiting Valve

question: Why must emergency and parking brakes on trucks, truck tractors, and buses be held on by mechanical force rather than air pressure?
choice_a: Mechanical force allows for a lighter vehicle
choice_b: Mechanical force is required by the alcohol evaporator system
choice_c: Air pressure would overheat the brake drums
choice_d: Air pressure can eventually leak away
explanation: Emergency and parking brakes must be held on by mechanical force because air pressure can eventually leak away.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.1.14 — Spring Brakes

question: Tractor and straight truck spring brakes will come fully on when air pressure drops to what range?
choice_a: 20-45 psi (typically 20-30 psi)
choice_d: 0-10 psi
explanation: Tractor and straight truck spring brakes come fully on when air pressure drops to a range of 20 to 45 psi, typically 20 to 30 psi.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.1.14 — Spring Brakes

question: What should you do when the low air pressure warning light and buzzer first come on?
choice_a: Wait for the spring brakes to engage on their own
choice_b: Bring the vehicle to a safe stop right away while you can still control the brakes
choice_c: Increase speed to reach a repair facility
choice_d: Shut off the engine immediately without stopping
explanation: The manual says not to wait for the brakes to come on automatically; instead, bring the vehicle to a safe stop right away while you can still control the brakes.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.1.14 — Spring Brakes

question: On newer vehicles with air brakes, what does the parking brake control knob look like?
choice_a: A round blue knob
choice_b: A square red button
choice_c: A diamond-shaped, yellow, push-pull knob
choice_d: A floor-mounted lever only
explanation: In newer vehicles, you put on the parking brakes using a diamond-shaped, yellow, push-pull control knob.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.1.15 — Parking Brake Controls

question: What caution does the manual give about pushing the brake pedal down when the spring brakes are on?
choice_a: It automatically resets the governor
choice_b: It has no effect on the vehicle
choice_c: It is required to release the spring brakes safely
choice_d: The brakes could be damaged by the combined forces of the springs and air pressure
explanation: Never push the brake pedal down when the spring brakes are on, as the brakes could be damaged by the combined forces of the springs and the air pressure.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.1.15 — Parking Brake Controls

question: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after what date are required to be equipped with antilock brakes (ABS)?
choice_a: March 1, 1997
choice_b: March 1, 1998
choice_c: January 1, 1997
choice_d: March 1, 2000
explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 are required to be equipped with antilock brakes.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.1.16 — Antilock Braking Systems (ABS)

question: What color are the ABS malfunction lamps found on tractors, trucks, buses, and trailers?
choice_a: Red
choice_b: Yellow
choice_c: Blue
choice_d: Green
explanation: Vehicles with ABS have yellow malfunction lamps to tell you if something isn't working.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.1.16 — Antilock Braking Systems (ABS)

question: What is a dual air brake system?
choice_a: A system with two separate brake pedals
choice_b: A single air system with a backup compressor
choice_c: Two separate air brake systems that use a single set of brake controls
choice_d: Two parking brakes mounted on one axle
explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate air brake systems, which use a single set of brake controls.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.2 — Dual Airbrake

question: In a dual air brake system, what does each of the two systems have separately?
choice_a: Only a shared brake pedal
choice_b: Only a shared parking brake control
choice_c: Its own engine and transmission
choice_d: Its own air tanks, hoses, lines, etc.
explanation: Each system in a dual air brake system has its own air tanks, hoses, lines, etc.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.2 — Dual Airbrake

question: In a typical dual air brake system, which axle does the "primary" system usually operate?
choice_a: The rear axle or axles
choice_b: The trailer axle only
choice_c: Both front and rear axles equally
choice_d: The front axle only
explanation: One system, called the primary system, typically operates the regular brakes on the rear axle or axles; the secondary system operates the front axle.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.2 — Dual Airbrake

question: Do both the primary and secondary systems in a dual air brake system supply air to the trailer, if there is one?
choice_a: No, only the primary system does
choice_b: Yes, both systems supply air to the trailer
choice_c: No, only the secondary system does
choice_d: Trailers use a fully independent air supply
explanation: Both the primary and secondary systems supply air to the trailer, if there is one.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.2 — Dual Airbrake

question: Before driving a vehicle with a dual air system, you should allow the compressor to build up a minimum pressure of what in both the primary and secondary systems?
choice_a: 60 psi
choice_b: 125 psi
choice_c: 100 psi
choice_d: 150 psi
explanation: Before driving, allow time for the air compressor to build up a minimum of 100 psi pressure in both the primary and secondary systems.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.2 — Dual Airbrake

question: The low air pressure warning light and buzzer should shut off when pressure in both systems rises to a manufacturer-set value that must be greater than what pressure?
choice_a: 40 psi
choice_b: 45 psi
choice_c: 100 psi
choice_d: 60 psi
explanation: The warning light and buzzer should shut off when air pressure in both systems rises to a manufacturer-set value that must be greater than 60 psi.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.2 — Dual Airbrake

question: The warning light and buzzer should come on before the air pressure drops below what level in either system?
choice_a: 60 psi
choice_b: 45 psi
choice_c: 90 psi
choice_d: 100 psi
explanation: The warning light and buzzer should come on before the air pressure drops below 60 psi in either system.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.2 — Dual Airbrake

question: If one air system in a dual air brake system becomes very low on pressure, what is the result?
choice_a: Nothing changes, since the other system fully compensates
choice_b: Either the front or rear brakes will not operate fully, increasing stopping distance
choice_c: The parking brake instantly and safely stops the vehicle
choice_d: The ABS fully compensates with no change in stopping distance
explanation: If one air system is very low on pressure, either the front or rear brakes will not be operating fully, meaning it will take longer to stop.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.2 — Dual Airbrake

question: What inspection procedure does the manual say should be used as the basis for inspecting a vehicle with air brakes?
choice_a: Only a visual walkaround with no other steps
choice_b: A specialized four-step airbrake-only procedure
choice_c: The basic seven-step inspection procedure described in Section 2
choice_d: The manufacturer's annual maintenance checklist
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to use the basic seven-step inspection procedure described in Section 2 to inspect a vehicle with air brakes.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.3 — Inspecting Airbrake Systems

question: During the Step 2 engine compartment check, what should you check if the air compressor is belt-driven?
choice_a: The alcohol evaporator fluid level
choice_b: The governor's cut-out pressure setting
choice_c: The tractor protection valve
choice_d: The condition and tightness of the drive belt
explanation: If the air compressor is belt-driven, check the condition and tightness of the belt during the Step 2 engine compartment check.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.3.1 — During Step 2 Engine Compartment Checks

question: How should you check a slack adjuster during the walkaround inspection?
choice_a: Chock the wheels, release the parking brake, and pull hard on each reachable slack adjuster by hand
choice_b: Read the application pressure gauge while driving
choice_c: Listen for a clicking sound while braking
choice_d: Check the ABS malfunction lamp only
explanation: Park on level ground, chock the wheels, release the parking brakes, and pull hard on each slack adjuster you can reach to check it.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.3.2 — During Step 5 Walkaround Inspection

question: If a slack adjuster moves more than about how far where the push rod attaches to it, it probably needs adjustment?
choice_a: Half an inch
choice_b: One inch
choice_c: Three inches
choice_d: Six inches
explanation: If a slack adjuster moves more than about one inch where the push rod attaches to it, it probably needs adjustment.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.3.2 — During Step 5 Walkaround Inspection

question: According to the manual, all vehicles built since what year have automatic slack adjustors?
explanation: The manual states that all vehicles built since 1991 have automatic slack adjustors.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.3.2 — During Step 5 Walkaround Inspection

question: Per the National Transportation Safety Board reference in the manual, why is manual adjustment of automatic slack adjusters considered dangerous?
choice_a: It voids the manufacturer's warranty
choice_b: It permanently disables the parking brake
choice_c: It is illegal under federal law in all cases
choice_d: It gives the vehicle operator a false sense of security about the braking system's effectiveness
explanation: According to the NTSB, manual adjustment of automatic slack adjusters is dangerous because it gives the vehicle operator a false sense of security about the effectiveness of the braking system.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.3.2 — During Step 5 Walkaround Inspection

question: Per the manual, brake drums (or discs) must not have cracks longer than what?
choice_a: One half the width of the friction area
choice_b: One quarter the width of the friction area
choice_c: The full width of the friction area
choice_d: Two inches, regardless of drum size
explanation: Brake drums (or discs) must not have cracks longer than one half the width of the friction area.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.3.2 — During Step 5 Walkaround Inspection

question: How do you test the low pressure warning signal during the Step 7 final airbrake check?
choice_a: Drive at highway speed while watching the gauge
choice_b: Shut off the engine, turn on electrical power, then step on and off the brake pedal until the warning activates
choice_c: Manually trigger the safety valve
choice_d: Disconnect the alcohol evaporator and observe the reaction
explanation: Shut the engine off with enough air pressure that the warning is not on, turn on electrical power, and step on and off the brake pedal to reduce tank pressure until the warning signal comes on.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.3.3 — Step 7 Final Airbrake Check

question: During the final inspection, the low air pressure warning signal must come on before the pressure drops to less than what level (or in the tank with the lowest pressure, in dual systems)?
choice_a: 45 psi
choice_b: 90 psi
choice_c: 60 psi
choice_d: 100 psi
explanation: The low air pressure warning signal must come on before the pressure drops to less than 60 psi in the air tank, or the tank with the lowest air pressure in dual systems.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.3.3 — Step 7 Final Airbrake Check

question: With a fully-charged air system, engine off, and parking brake released, what is the maximum acceptable air pressure loss rate for a single vehicle?
choice_a: Less than one psi per minute
choice_b: Less than five psi per minute
choice_c: Less than three psi per minute
choice_d: Less than two psi per minute
explanation: The static air loss rate should be less than two psi in one minute for single vehicles.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.3.3 — Step 7 Final Airbrake Check

question: Under the same static leakage test, what is the maximum acceptable loss rate for a combination vehicle?
choice_a: Less than three psi per minute
choice_b: Less than one psi per minute
choice_c: Less than two psi per minute
choice_d: Less than four psi per minute
explanation: The static air loss rate should be less than three psi in one minute for combination vehicles.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.3.3 — Step 7 Final Airbrake Check

question: After applying 90 psi or more with the brake pedal, what is the maximum acceptable air loss rate for a single vehicle?
choice_a: Less than one psi in one minute
choice_b: Less than three psi in one minute
choice_c: Less than five psi in one minute
choice_d: Less than six psi in one minute
explanation: After applying 90 psi or more with the brake pedal, if air pressure falls more than three psi in one minute for single vehicles, the air loss rate is too much.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.3.3 — Step 7 Final Airbrake Check

question: After applying 90 psi or more with the brake pedal, what is the maximum acceptable air loss rate for a combination vehicle?
choice_a: Less than three psi in one minute
choice_b: Less than two psi in one minute
choice_c: Less than four psi in one minute
choice_d: Less than six psi in one minute
explanation: After applying 90 psi or more, more than four psi in one minute for combination vehicles means the air loss rate is too much.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.3.3 — Step 7 Final Airbrake Check

question: During the final airbrake check, pumping by the air compressor should start (cut-in) at about what pressure and stop (cut-out) at about what pressure?
choice_a: Start at 60 psi, stop at 90 psi
choice_b: Start at 45 psi, stop at 100 psi
choice_c: Start at 125 psi, stop at 150 psi
choice_d: Start at about 100 psi, stop at about 125 psi
explanation: Pumping by the air compressor should start at about 100 psi and stop at about 125 psi, checked at a fast idle.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.3.3 — Step 7 Final Airbrake Check

question: During the final check, at what pressure range should the tractor protection valve and parking brake valve close ("pop out"), causing the spring brakes to come on?
choice_d: 0-20 psi
explanation: The tractor protection valve and parking brake valve should close (pop out) when air pressure falls to the manufacturer's specification, 20 to 45 psi.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.3.3 — Step 7 Final Airbrake Check

question: In dual air systems, at operating rpm, the air pressure should build from 85 to 100 psi within how many seconds?
choice_a: 25 seconds
choice_b: 45 seconds
choice_c: 90 seconds
choice_d: 180 seconds
explanation: When the engine is at operating rpms, pressure should build from 85 to 100 psi within 45 seconds in dual air systems.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.3.3 — Step 7 Final Airbrake Check

question: In single air systems (pre-1975), typical requirements are pressure buildup from 50 to 90 psi within how many minutes, at an idle speed of 600-900 rpm?
choice_a: 1 minute
choice_b: 5 minutes
choice_c: 3 minutes
choice_d: 10 minutes
explanation: In single air systems (pre-1975), typical requirements are pressure buildup from 50 to 90 psi within 3 minutes at an idle speed of 600-900 rpm.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.3.3 — Step 7 Final Airbrake Check

question: How do you test the parking brake during the final airbrake check?
choice_a: Drive at highway speed and apply it suddenly
choice_b: Check only the dashboard indicator light
choice_c: Release the parking brake and observe the air pressure drop
choice_d: Stop the vehicle, apply the parking brake, and gently pull against it in a low gear
explanation: To test the parking brake, stop the vehicle, put the parking brake on, and gently pull against it in a low gear to test that it holds.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.3.3 — Step 7 Final Airbrake Check

question: How do you test the service brakes during the final airbrake check?
choice_a: Test only while the vehicle is parked
choice_b: Apply the parking brake and check for smoke
choice_c: Check the alcohol evaporator fluid level
choice_d: Move the vehicle forward slowly (about five mph) and apply the brakes firmly, noting any pulling or delayed stopping
explanation: To test service brakes, move the vehicle forward slowly (about five mph) and apply the brakes firmly, noting any pulling, unusual feel, or delayed stopping action.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.3.3 — Step 7 Final Airbrake Check

question: With a manual transmission, when should you push the clutch in during a normal stop?
choice_a: Immediately as you begin braking
choice_b: Not until the engine rpm is down close to idle
choice_c: Only after the vehicle has fully stopped
choice_d: Never, air brakes require holding the clutch throughout
explanation: With a manual transmission, don't push the clutch in until the engine rpm is down close to idle.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.4.1 — Normal Stops

question: What does the ABS computer do when it senses impending wheel lockup?
choice_a: It applies the parking brake automatically
choice_b: It shuts off the engine
choice_c: It reduces the braking pressure to a safe level
choice_d: It opens the safety relief valve
explanation: The ABS computer senses impending lockup, reduces the braking pressure to a safe level, and you maintain control.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.4.2 — Braking with Antilock Brakes

question: Does ABS necessarily shorten your stopping distance?
choice_a: Yes, it always cuts stopping distance in half
choice_b: Yes, but only on wet pavement
choice_c: No, and it provides no benefit to vehicle control
choice_d: Not necessarily, but it helps you keep the vehicle under control during hard braking
explanation: ABS does not necessarily shorten your stopping distance, but it does help you keep the vehicle under control during hard braking.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.4.2 — Braking with Antilock Brakes

question: When only the tractor has ABS (not the trailer), what benefit does the manual describe?
choice_a: You should be able to maintain steering control, with less chance of jackknifing
choice_b: The trailer is guaranteed not to swing out
choice_c: Stopping distance is cut significantly
choice_d: The trailer brakes lock automatically for stability
explanation: When only the tractor has ABS, you should be able to maintain steering control, and there is less chance of jackknifing.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.4.2 — Braking with Antilock Brakes

question: When only the trailer has ABS (not the tractor), what does the manual advise if you lose steering control or start a tractor jackknife?
choice_a: Immediately apply the parking brake
choice_b: Let up on the brakes, if you can safely do so, until you gain control
choice_c: Apply the trailer brakes fully and hold
choice_d: Increase brake pressure to force the trailer straight
explanation: When only the trailer has ABS, if you lose steering control or start a tractor jackknife, let up on the brakes if you can safely do so until you gain control.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.4.2 — Braking with Antilock Brakes

question: What is the one exception the manual describes to braking the same way regardless of whether ABS is on the tractor, trailer, or both?
choice_a: Never fully apply the brakes even in emergencies
choice_b: Brake only with the trailer brakes when ABS is present
choice_c: In an emergency stop, with working ABS on all axles of a straight truck or combination, you can fully apply the brakes
choice_d: Always use stab braking when ABS is present
explanation: The one exception: if you always drive a straight truck or combination with working ABS on all axles, in an emergency stop you can fully apply the brakes.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.4.2 — Braking with Antilock Brakes

question: What is the "controlled braking" method of emergency stopping?
choice_a: Alternately pumping the brake pedal rapidly
choice_b: Using only the parking brake to stop
choice_c: Releasing the brakes completely and coasting to a stop
choice_d: Applying the brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels, using small steering movements
explanation: With controlled braking, you apply the brakes as hard as you can without locking the wheels, keeping steering wheel movements very small.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.4.3 — Emergency Stops

question: What is the "stab braking" method of emergency stopping?
choice_a: Applying the brakes all the way, releasing when the wheels lock up, and reapplying fully once they start rolling again
choice_b: Using only the trailer brakes
choice_c: Alternating between service brake and parking brake
choice_d: Gradually increasing brake pressure over ten seconds
explanation: Stab braking means applying your brakes all the way, releasing when wheels lock up, then applying fully again as soon as the wheels start rolling.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.4.3 — Emergency Stops

question: When using stab braking, how long can it take for the wheels to start rolling again after you release the brakes?
choice_a: There is no delay at all
choice_b: Up to one second
choice_c: Up to five seconds
choice_d: Up to ten seconds
explanation: It can take up to one second for the wheels to start rolling after you release the brakes in stab braking.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.4.3 — Emergency Stops

question: What is "brake lag" in an air brake system?
choice_a: The time it takes the driver to perceive a hazard
choice_b: The delay before ABS activates
choice_c: The time required for the brakes to work after the brake pedal is pushed
choice_d: The time for the parking brake to release
explanation: Brake lag is the added delay that is the time required for the brakes to work after the brake pedal is pushed.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.4.4 — Stopping Distance

question: How much time does brake lag typically take for air to flow through the lines to the brakes?
choice_a: Instantly, with no delay
choice_b: Five seconds or more
choice_c: Ten seconds or more
choice_d: One half second or more
explanation: With air brakes it takes a little time, one half second or more, for the air to flow through the lines to the brakes.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.4.4 — Stopping Distance

question: What four factors make up total stopping distance for a vehicle with air brakes, according to the manual?
choice_a: Perception Distance + Reaction Distance + Brake Lag Distance + Braking Distance
choice_b: Perception Distance + Governor Distance + Compressor Distance + Braking Distance
choice_c: Reaction Distance + Alcohol Evaporator Distance + Brake Lag Distance + Stopping Distance
choice_d: Perception Distance + Reaction Distance + Parking Distance + Braking Distance
explanation: Total stopping distance equals Perception Distance + Reaction Distance + Brake Lag Distance + Braking Distance.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.4.4 — Stopping Distance

question: About how many additional feet does the air brake lag distance add at 55 mph on dry pavement?
choice_a: 10 feet
choice_b: 32 feet
choice_c: 60 feet
choice_d: 100 feet
explanation: The airbrake lag distance at 55 mph on dry pavement adds about 32 feet.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.4.4 — Stopping Distance

question: At 55 mph, under good traction and brake conditions, what is the approximate total stopping distance for an average driver in a vehicle with air brakes?
choice_a: Over 200 feet
choice_b: Over 300 feet
choice_c: Over 450 feet
choice_d: Over 600 feet
explanation: At 55 mph for an average driver under good traction and brake conditions, the total stopping distance is over 450 feet.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.4.4 — Stopping Distance

question: What causes brake fade according to the manual?
choice_a: Cold weather freezing the brake lines
choice_b: A malfunctioning alcohol evaporator
choice_c: Low air compressor cut-in pressure
choice_d: Excessive heat from overuse of the service brakes causing chemical changes in the brake lining
explanation: Excessive use of the service brakes results in overheating and leads to brake fade from chemical changes in the brake lining that reduce friction.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.4.5 — Brake Fading or Failure

question: When using the proper technique for braking on a long, steep downgrade, when should you release the brakes?
choice_a: When your speed has been reduced to about 5 mph below your "safe" speed
choice_b: As soon as you begin to slow down
choice_c: Only at the bottom of the grade
choice_d: Never release until the grade ends
explanation: Apply the brakes until your speed is reduced to about 5 mph below your safe speed, then release; this application should last about three seconds.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.4.6 — Proper Braking Technique

question: Why does a heavily loaded vehicle take a long distance to stop once the spring brakes engage due to low air pressure?
choice_a: Because the ABS disengages entirely
choice_b: Because the spring brakes do not work on all axles
choice_c: Because spring brakes apply too much force
choice_d: Because the alcohol evaporator empties
explanation: A heavily loaded vehicle will take a long distance to stop with spring brakes on because the spring brakes do not work on all axles.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.4.7 — Low Air Pressure

question: What does the manual say you should never do when leaving your vehicle unattended?
choice_a: Leave the windows open
choice_b: Leave the engine running
choice_c: Leave without applying the parking brakes or chocking the wheels
choice_d: Leave without checking the ABS lamp
explanation: Never leave your vehicle unattended without applying the parking brakes or chocking the wheels, or it might roll away and cause injury and damage.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 5.4.8 — Parking Brakes
